s1.syndrome_frame: Postpartum headache with worsening course and associated symptoms
salient_findings: Layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection on noncontrast CT
key_facts: 31 days postpartum after elective cesarean delivery
Initial mild global headache 8 days postoperatively
Normal prothrombin time, partial prothrombin time, and international normalized ratio
Noncontrast CT showed extra-axial collection with areas of linear and crescentic hyperdensity

shortlist.label: Subdural hematoma
shortlist.why_kept: Noncontrast CT showed extra-axial collection with areas of linear and crescentic hyperdensity, consistent with subdural hematoma

shortlist.label: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension
shortlist.why_kept: Postpartum headache with worsening course, normal vital signs, and intact motor function, consistent with spontaneous intracranial hypotension

shortlist.label: Postpartum cerebral vasculopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Postpartum headache with worsening course, normal laboratory studies, and noncontrast CT findings, consistent with postpartum cerebral vasculopathy

shortlist.label: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Postpartum headache with worsening course, normal vital signs, and noncontrast CT findings, consistent with reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome

shortlist.label: Dural sinus thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Noncontrast CT showed extra-axial collection with areas of linear and crescentic hyperdensity, and postpartum state increases risk of thrombosis

raw.rationale: The noncontrast CT of the head revealed a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection, which is consistent with a subdural hematoma, especially given the history of recent cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia and the progression of headache severity.

rejected.label: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension
rejected.why: Typically presents with postural headache, which is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Postpartum cerebral vasculopathy
rejected.why: Usually presents with seizures, hypertension, and other systemic symptoms, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome
rejected.why: Typically presents with thunderclap headache and is often associated with vasoconstriction on imaging, which is not described here

rejected.label: Dural sinus thrombosis
rejected.why: Would likely show hyperdensity in a venous sinus on CT, which is not mentioned in the imaging findings
